title: How Salt Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore salt: the origin of salty idioms (not worth his salt, salary, salad, grain of salt), salt's history as currency and preservation, Gandhi's Salt March, the Erie Canal and salt, salt in the Civil War, and salt's role in the body (electrolytes, hyponatremia and hypernatremia). They cover the health debate over sodium intake, the chemistry of sodium chloride, types of salt (table salt with iodine and anti-caking agents, the Morton Salt girl ad, sea salt, fleur de sel, pink Himalayan and Hawaiian alaea, black lava salt, smoked salt, kosher and rock salt), and three mining methods (deep shaft room-and-pillar, solution mining, solar evaporation), including the Wieliczka Salt Mine. The episode closes with a listener mail from Glenn, a Southern California police officer, correcting an error about the Christopher Dorner manhunt shootings, and a sponsor read for Lynda.com.

segments.title: Opening banter and salty idioms
segments.summary: The hosts open by discussing the word salty and origins of salt idioms such as taking something with a grain of salt, not being worth one's salt, and the etymology of salary and salad.

segments.title: Salt history, currency and Gandhi's Salt March
segments.summary: Salt's historical importance: ancient trade, economies and control of salt production, Gandhi's 240-mile Salt March against British control of salt in India, and salt as currency in Ethiopia and as a method of suicide among Chinese nobility.

segments.title: Salt preservation and curing
segments.summary: Salt's role in preserving food by drawing out moisture and killing bacteria, which is the basis of curing meat, and the sodium in packaged foods.

segments.title: Salt in medieval Europe, American colonies, and the Erie Canal
segments.summary: Medieval tortures including the goat's tongue, the Old Salt Route in northern Germany, the Massachusetts Bay Colony salt works, and the Erie Canal being built largely to transport salt.

segments.title: Salt in the Civil War
segments.summary: Salt's role in Union strategy during the Civil War, with battles over salt works and mines such as Saltville, Virginia, and the salt shortage's effect on Confederate morale.

segments.title: Salt, electrolytes and the body
segments.summary: Salt is essential to the body; humans have a taste for it, and it carries electrical impulses for muscles and the heart. Discussion of hyponatremia from too little salt (water intoxication, diuretics, vomiting) and hypernatremia from too much, with its effect on blood volume and blood pressure.

segments.title: Sodium intake guidelines and the health debate
segments.summary: Recommended sodium limits (about 2.4 grams per day), average American intake, and the CDC panel finding that cutting sodium does not clearly reduce heart attack or stroke risk, with low and high intake groups at higher risk.

segments.title: Types of salt: table salt and iodine
segments.summary: Table salt is the most common salt, refined with anti-caking agents. Iodization was added to prevent goiter and developmental problems, and is linked to the Flynn effect. The Morton Salt girl ad with the umbrella slogan 'when it rains it pours' is described.

segments.title: Sea salt, colored and smoked salts
segments.summary: Sea salt, fleur de sel harvested by hand in France, pink Himalayan salt and the algae coloring, Hawaiian alaea with iron oxide, black lava salt, gray Celtic salt, and smoked salt.

segments.title: Kosher salt and rock salt
segments.summary: Kosher salt is not kosher itself but is used to draw blood from meat to make it kosher; its coarse grain means it must be doubled when substituting for table salt. Rock salt is unrefined and used for de-icing and ice cream.

segments.title: Salt mining methods and famous salt mines
segments.summary: Top salt producers (China, US, Germany, India, Australia). Three mining methods: deep shaft room-and-pillar mining, solution mining by pumping water into salt beds and evaporating brine, and solar evaporation. The Wieliczka Salt Mine in Poland with its salt cathedral and chandeliers.

segments.title: Religious significance of salt
segments.summary: Salt's religious and symbolic role: Lot's wife turned into a pillar of salt in the Old Testament, a salt pillar near Mount Ararat, the custom of keeping salt in cars for protection, and a quote from Roman senator Cassiodorus.

segments.title: Sponsor plug for local homemade salts
segments.summary: Chuck plugs a Atlanta maker of handcrafted sea salts, including the Magic Unicorn blend, and gives contact details.

segments.title: Listener mail: Christopher Dorner manhunt correction
segments.summary: Listener Glenn, a Southern California police officer, corrects an episode error about the Christopher Dorner manhunt: the LAPD fired on one vehicle and the Torrance Police Department on another, and he says nobody was killed. Josh says he will recheck and admit any error.

segments.title: Lynda.com sponsor read and outro
segments.summary: Sponsor read for Lynda.com online video tutorials, followed by contact information and sign-off.
